(prefektura)|wuu|爱知县|zh|愛知縣|zh_classical|愛知縣|zh_min_nan|Aiti-koān|zh_yue|愛知縣|qid=Q80434}}. {{nihongo|'''Ishimaki Shrine'''|石巻神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mikawa Province]].

It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} (Ishimaki Shrine of Yana District, {{ill|Mikawa Province|ar|مقاطعة ميكاوا|ckb|پارێزگای میکاوا|cs|Provincie Mikawa|de|Provinz Mikawa|eo|Provinco Mikaŭa|es|Provincia de Mikawa|fa|ولایت میکاوا|fi|Mikawan provinssi|fr|Province de Mikawa|gl|Provincia de Mikawa|hak|Mikawa-koet|id|Provinsi Mikawa|it|Mikawa (provincia)|ja|三河国|ko|미카와국|lt|Mikavos žemė|nl|Mikawa (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Mikawa|pt|Província de Mikawa|ru|Микава (провинция)|simple|Mikawa Province|sk|Mikawa|sr|Провинција Микава|th|แคว้นมิกาวะ|tr|Mikawa (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Мікава|ur|میکاوا صوبہ|zh|三河國|zh_classical|三河國|zh_min_nan|Mikawa-kok|zh_yue|三河國|qid=Q768158}}). Its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Gō-sha|Q134917316|qid=Q134917316}}, and it is regarded as the fourth shrine of Mikawa Province{{要出典|date=April 2014}}.

== Overview ==
The founding period is unknown. It is also said to date to the era of {{ill|Emperor Kōan|ar|الإمبراطور كوان|arz|الامبراطور كوان|azb|کوان (ایمپیراتور)|ca|Kōan|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر کۆوان|cs|Kóan (císař)|de|Kōan (Tennō)|eo|Koan|es|Kōan Tennō|fa|امپراتور کوآن|fi|Kōan (keisari)|fr|Kōan (empereur)|he|קואן, קיסר יפן|hr|Kōan (japanski car)|hu|Kóan japán császár|id|Kaisar Kōan|it|Kōan (imperatore del Giappone)|ja|孝安天皇|ka|კოანი|ko|고안 천황|lt|Imperatorius Koanas|ms|Maharaja Kōan|nl|Koan (keizer)|pl|Kōan|pt|Koan (imperador)|ru|Император Коан|sh|Car Kōan|simple|Emperor Kōan|sl|Cesar Koan|sr|Коан (јапански цар)|sv|Koan (kejsare)|th|จักรพรรดิโคอัง|tl|Emperador Koan|tr|Kōan (imparator)|uk|Імператор Коан|uz|Imperator Kōan|vi|Thiên hoàng Kōan|zh|孝安天皇|zh_min_nan|Kôan Thian-hông|zh_yue|孝安天皇|qid=Q312821}} or {{ill|Empress Suiko|Q298057|qid=Q298057}}. Originally, {{ill|Mount Ishimaki|Q11586461|qid=Q11586461}} itself is presumed to have been an object of worship.

Because it lay on the northeast demon gate of {{ill|Yoshida Castle (Mikawa Province)|Q849190|qid=Q849190|lt=Yoshida Castle}}, it is said to have received devotion from successive castle lords since the castle’s construction.

It is divided between the okumiya (upper shrine) on the mid-slope of Mount Ishimaki and the satomiya (lower shrine) in the mountain village. The upper shrine holds the Kuda-gayu rite, and the lower shrine holds the Oni festival.

== Enshrined deity ==
{{ill|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|qid=Q276944|lt=Ōnamuchi-no-Mikoto}}

== Festivals ==
== Kuda-gayu Festival ==
A rite held at the Ishimaki Shrine okumiya on lunar January 15 (early February in the solar calendar) to divine agricultural fortune.

The priest recites norito, lights the ritual firewood at the hearth with flint, and cooks porridge in a pot. Eighteen reed tubes labeled with crop names are placed into the boiling porridge and stirred with {{ill|Cleyera japonica|Q775470|qid=Q775470}} branches. After about one hour, the tubes are removed and crop fortune is divined from the state of porridge inside each tube.

== Oni Festival ==
Annual festival held at the satomiya on the first Sunday of April. Also called the “chimaki festival” or “doburoku festival.”

It is said to have begun when an oni mask was dedicated in thanks for prayers for recovery of {{ill|Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800|qid=Q242800}}.

Worshippers are served {{ill|Zongzi|Q713466|qid=Q713466}} and {{ill|Doburoku|Q1371541|qid=Q1371541}}. The oni of this festival are a black oni and a red oni, regarded as divine manifestations. They rampage in the precincts and scatter white powder containing candy; receiving the powder is said to prevent colds. If one fails to evade the oni, one may be showered with a large amount of powder from a can.

== Access ==
* From {{ill|Toyohashi Station|Q771465|qid=Q771465}} ({{ill|Central Japan Railway Company|Q513679|qid=Q513679|lt=JR}} {{ill|Tōkaidō Line (JR Central)|Q11235139|qid=Q11235139|lt=Tōkaidō Main Line}}, {{ill|Iida Line|Q771305|qid=Q771305}}, {{ill|Meitetsu|Q30850|qid=Q30850}} {{ill|Meitetsu Nagoya Main Line|Q1137838|qid=Q1137838}}), take {{ill|Toyotetsu Bus|Q11634286|qid=Q11634286}} Toyohashi-Wada-tsuji line and get off at “Ishimaki Tozanguchi.”
